__doc__: TENANT-NEUTRAL EXAMPLE. Placeholder ids only — never real ones.
This file documents the SHAPE of settings.sync_registry. It is never applied.
The real registry for a deployment lives at data/registry/sync_registry.json,
which is gitignored for the same reason .env is: it holds one client's
connection ids and live Drive folder ids.
Gate G40 (scripts/refactor/fixture-live-key-lint.py) bars `sync_registry` from
any blueprint fixture, after a 2026-08-05 incident where a fixture's registry row
was upserted over a real client's live registry twice, deleting two configured
drive pipes and blanking `connection` on two more. A tracked file holding real
folder ids would also point the NEXT deployment bootstrapped from this repo at
THIS client's Drive on its very first seed — a cross-tenant leak, not just an
overwrite. Hence: shape here, values out of tree.
regenerate the real file   apps/indox/hooks/sync-registry-converge.py --emit
preview a convergence      ... --dry-run
prove the contract offline ... --selftest
RUNTIME KEYS ARE NEVER STORED HERE. last_run / last_run_execution / last_run_url
are written by the engine; convergence preserves whatever the live row holds and
never seeds or clears them. See RUNTIME_KEYS in the hook — the one definition.
`feedback` — DERIVED, not hand-written. It says whether the state machine reports a
document's VERDICT back to the source: moving the Drive file into the pair's `synced`
or `failed` folder, or adding the pipe's `labels.synced` / `labels.failed` tag to the
mail. Convergence materialises an explicit block for every pipe from the vocabulary
the entry already declares (see feedback_for() in sync-registry-converge.py, proved by
--selftest section 7), so turning feedback on for a pipe means GIVING IT SOMEWHERE TO
FILE, not setting a flag in a second place. A pipe whose `synced` and `failed` are the
same folder cannot express a verdict and is derived to mode 'off' with the reason in
`_derived`. Write the block by hand only to OVERRIDE the derivation; an explicit block
always wins. Consumers treat an ABSENT block as off, so a pipe authored through the
Console does nothing until convergence gives it one.
THE 2026-09-02 CONTRACT (owner rule): a pipe REQUIRES only its source — the drive pair's
`to_sync` folder, or the gmail `labels.to_sync` tag. `synced` / `failed` folders and tags
are OPTIONAL user-visible marks the state machine's feedback writes; sync state itself
lives in sync_ledger (the sync item) and never depends on where a file or mail sits.
`dest_folder` (gmail: where attachments are saved) defaults to the drive's root when
absent. processor_wf / v3_mode / claim_label / search_take are RETIRED: every pipe is
thin v3, and the engine does not claim by label.

pairs.__doc__: Both vocabularies are written by _normalise_entry: the editor/sim uses from/to/failed_to, the engine uses to_sync/synced/failed. Every pipe needs its OWN synced and failed folders — sharing them across pipes was a live three-way collision. Replace every PLACEHOLDER_* with a real Drive folder id.

batch._chunk: ONE IMAP connection per mailbox is the rule, so chunk bounds how many deliveries queue on it per pass (each attachment fetch is tens of seconds; the mail workflow waits up to 300 s) — measured 2026-09-02: 25 parallel fetches aborted the queued ones
